ranking.name: Air temperature near the ground
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, air temperature near the ground in Mexico changed by +0.203 °C per decade (95% confidence interval +0.105 to +0.299), which is statistically significant (p < 0.001). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is an increase of about 0.500 °C.

cautions: The confidence interval is wide compared with the trend, so the size of the change is uncertain.
ranking.name: Water in the topsoil
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water in the topsoil in Mexico changed by −0.19 kg/m² per decade (95% confidence interval −0.37 to 0.00), which is statistically significant (p = 0.04). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is a decrease of about 0.46 kg/m².

ranking.name: Rain and snow (precipitation)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, rain and snow (precipitation) in Mexico shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.24): the estimate is +0.032 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.022 to +0.085). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.

ranking.name: Water running off the surface
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water running off the surface in Mexico shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.46): the estimate is −0.004 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.015 to +0.007). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.

ranking.name: Water leaving the land (evapotranspiration)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water leaving the land (evapotranspiration) in Mexico shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.61): the estimate is +0.004 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.012 to +0.020). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.
